mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 3.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses wage growth and consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 6-month averages signals a robust demand environment, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and inflation, ultimately leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to higher corporate pricing power.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change < -1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
